topIssues.title: create a new op-spammer component for deployment in devnets
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
For v0, this would be a simple service which can be configured with a private key and ethereum RPC endpoint, and periodically sends any kind of user transaction to that endpoint. 

This would help catch bugs on devnets which are all-too-often completely devoid of any kind of user traffic. This obscures problems and delays the discovery of bugs until we hit production networks. 

This would be a good candidate to be written in Rust for any beginner Rustacean looking for a small task to onboard with. 

Extensions for a v1:
* cycles through all transaction _types_ (setCode, legacy, ...)
* fuzzes the `calldata`, `to`, `amount` fields
* maintains a high load of transactions, enough to fill blocks to 50%, 100%
* optimizes for recovering funds / not needing constant topups
* can be controlled over an RPC
* can be configured to send "spam" (calldata heavy transactions) or compute-heavy transactions (it could CREATE2 deploy a contract which allows for heavy compute and send transactions there).

topIssues.title: Supernode: Finalized Label SuperAuthorization
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
Following from:

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18976

Now, when the CL attempts to mark some block finalized by its rules, we must also block it by additional rules:

https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Supervisor-V2-Main-Loop-and-Logic-Flow-Diagrams-265f153ee162804388dac933f525de7b

The node will appear with an L2/L1 block to finalize, and we will need to make sure that verification is complete **considerate of that L1**. What this means is:

- Every Verification Activity stores a notion of the latest L2 timestamp it verified, the L2 heads, and importantly - The L1 block used to do so
- When finalization would occur in the Virtual Node, the SuperAuthority can be consulted `CanFinalize?`
- Chain Container can satisfy that query by consulting the Verifications and ensuring that the L2 block is correct, and the L1 block is known to be in the verified range for all Verifiers

Like other authority signals, a simple approve/deny is returned, and the node simply does not finalize data which it is not permitted to.

topIssues.title: ci: kona-client fails check-cross-platform-rust smoke test (--version)
topIssues.author: falcorocks
topIssues.body:
## `kona-client` fails `check-cross-platform-rust` smoke test (`--version`)

### Summary

Since PR #19246 was merged, the `develop` branch build has been failing consistently. The `check-cross-platform-rust` job runs `docker run $IMAGE --version` against all Rust images, but `kona-client` does not support this, it has no CLI argument handling.

### Error

```
Program encountered fatal error: OracleProviderError(Preimage(IOError(Closed)))
```

Both `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners are affected.

### Why it happens

`kona-client` is a `#![no_std]` binary that runs inside a Fault Proof VM. It uses the `#[client_entry]` proc macro and has no `clap` or argument parsing. When invoked with `--version`, it ignores the flag, tries to connect to oracle file descriptors that don't exist outside the VM, and crashes.

Other Rust images (`kona-host`, `kona-node`, `op-rbuilder`, `op-reth`) all pass because they use `clap` with `#[command(version)]`.

### Affected runs

All `develop` builds since `3019251` (Feb 19):
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/22190576223
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/22196666685
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/22209025663
- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/actions/runs/22209553750

### Suggested short term fix

Remove `kona-client` from the `check-cross-platform-rust` matrix and its corresponding `check-cross-platform` exclude entry in `.github/workflows/branches.yaml`. The image can still be built and pushed... it just can't be smoke-tested with `--version`.

topPRs.title: feat(flashblocks): enable speculative building on pending blocks (3)
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Enable building flashblocks on top of pending blocks before their canonical parent arrives via P2P, reducing latency when flashblocks arrive faster than canonical blocks.

Part of the [speculative flashblock building design](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Flashblocks-Upstreaming-node-reth-features-2e8f153ee162805eaaa5f067fe3440a3?source=copy_link). Builds on [PR 2](https://github.com/op-rs/op-reth/pull/591), and will rebase to target https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth once it merges.

## Motivation

The sequence manager currently discards flashblocks whose parent hash doesn't match the canonical tip. This means flashblocks for block N+1 sit idle until block N propagates via P2P—negating the latency advantage of the WebSocket feed.

With speculative building, we track execution state from previous builds and use it as prestate for subsequent builds, allowing continuous flashblock processing without waiting for P2P.

## Changes

**`pending_state.rs`** (new)
- `PendingBlockState<N>` - Tracks block hash, number, parent hash, execution outcome, and cached reads from a build
- `PendingStateRegistry<N>` - Stores most recent pending state for use by subsequent builds

**`cache.rs`**
- Extend `next_buildable_args()` with 3-priority build selection:
  1. Canonical-Pending: pending sequence parent matches canonical tip
  2. Canonical-Cached: cached sequence parent matches canonical tip  
  3. Speculative: pending/cached sequence parent matches pending state's block hash
- Add `pending_parent` field to `BuildArgs`

**`worker.rs`**
- Accept optional `pending_parent` in `BuildArgs`
- Use `with_bundle_prestate()` to overlay pending state's bundle on the canonical state provider
- Return `PendingBlockState` in `BuildResult` for use by subsequent builds

**`service.rs`**
- Add `PendingStateRegistry` field
- Record pending state after successful builds
- Pass pending state to `next_buildable_args()`
- Clear pending states on reconciliation
- Add `with_speculative_building()` opt-in (disabled by default)

## Testing

New integration test harness in `tests/it/`:
- `harness.rs` - `FlashBlockServiceTestHarness`, `TestSequenceManager`, `TestFlashBlockFactory`
- `service.rs` - Tests for speculative build priority, canonical precedence, pending state registry, depth limits

topPRs.title: op-devstack: add unified Registry for component storage (Phase 2)
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
This PR introduces a unified `Registry` type for op-devstack that can replace the 14+ separate `locks.RWMap` instances currently used in the Orchestrator. This is Phase 2 of the ID type system refactor.

### Problem

The current Orchestrator maintains separate registries for each component type:

```go
type Orchestrator struct {
    batchers        locks.RWMap[stack.L2BatcherID, *L2Batcher]
    proposers       locks.RWMap[stack.L2ProposerID, *L2Proposer]
    challengers     locks.RWMap[stack.L2ChallengerID, *L2Challenger]
    l2ELs           locks.RWMap[stack.L2ELNodeID, L2ELNode]
    rollupBoosts    locks.RWMap[stack.RollupBoostNodeID, *RollupBoostNode]
    // ... 9 more
}
```

This leads to:
- No unified way to query "all components on chain X"
- Manual polymorphic lookups (checking multiple registries)
- Adding new component types requires new registry fields

### Solution

A single `Registry` with secondary indexes:

```go
type Registry struct {
    components map[ComponentID]any           // Primary storage
    byKind     map[ComponentKind][]ComponentID  // "All batchers"
    byChainID  map[eth.ChainID][]ComponentID    // "All on chain 420"
}
```

Type-safe access via generic functions:

```go
// Register and retrieve with compile-time type safety
RegistryRegister(r, batcherID, batcher)
batcher, ok := RegistryGet[*L2Batcher](r, batcherID)

// Query by kind or chain
batchers := RegistryGetByKind[*L2Batcher](r, KindL2Batcher)
components := RegistryGetByChainID[*L2Batcher](r, chainID)
```

### Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `stack/registry.go` | Unified Registry implementation |
| `stack/registry_test.go` | Comprehensive test suite (21 tests) |
| `stack/component_id.go` | Added `HasChainID()` helper |
| [Design document](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Devstack-ID-Type-System-Refactor-2eef153ee1628048bb7ade1030fe6e9b) | Phase 2 implementation notes |

### Test Plan

- [x] Basic CRUD operations (Register, Get, Has, Unregister)
- [x] Secondary index queries (GetByKind, GetByChainID)
- [x] All three ID shapes (key+chain, chain-only, key-only)
- [x] Replace behavior (same ID registered twice)
- [x] Index cleanup on unregister
- [x] Concurrent access safety
- [x] Type-safe generic accessors
- [x] Range iteration with early termination

### Migration Path

This is non-breaking. The Registry can coexist with existing `locks.RWMap` fields:

1. Orchestrator can optionally maintain a Registry alongside existing maps
2. New code can use Registry, old code continues using maps
3. Phase 3 will add capability interfaces for polymorphic lookups
4. Phase 4 will migrate Orchestrator to use Registry exclusively

topPRs.title: test(contracts): improve DelayedWETH test coverage with fuzz tests
topPRs.author: devin-ai-integration
topPRs.body:
# test(contracts): convert DelayedWETH tests to fuzz and add coverage

## Summary

Enhances `DelayedWETH.t.sol` by converting 12 focused tests to fuzz tests and adding 2 new tests for previously uncovered code paths.

**Fuzz conversions (12 tests):**
- `unlock`: fuzz sub-account address and amounts; fuzz double-unlock with variable amounts and time deltas
- `withdraw` (both 1-arg and 2-arg overloads): fuzz deposit/withdraw amounts, fuzz time-before-delay, fuzz over-withdrawal amounts
- `hold`: fuzz hold amounts for both overloads; fuzz non-owner address for access control
- `recover`: fuzz non-owner address for access control

**New coverage (2 tests):**
- `testFuzz_recover_partialAmount_succeeds` — covers the `_wad < address(this).balance` branch in `recover()`, which was previously untested (only full-balance and over-balance recovery had coverage)
- `test_version_validFormat_succeeds` — validates `version()` returns a parseable semver string via `SemverComp.parse()`

No tests were removed. Tests that target specific scenarios (paused, locked with timestamp=0) were left as focused tests.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Fuzz bounds correctness**: Verify `bound()` ranges won't cause overflow or vacuous passes — particularly `_wad1 + _wad2` (both `uint128.max`), `_deposit + _extra` (both `uint192.max`), and `_timeBefore` bounded to `delayedWeth.delay()` (assumes delay > 0)
- [ ] **`vm.deal` replacing balance**: Fuzzed withdraw/hold tests use `vm.deal(alice, _wad)` which *sets* alice's ETH balance rather than relying on the pre-existing 10000 ether from setUp — confirm this doesn't mask any edge case the originals caught
- [ ] **Partial recovery test**: `testFuzz_recover_partialAmount_succeeds` bounds `_wad` to `[0, _balance - 1)` — verify this correctly exercises the `amount = _wad` path (not `amount = address(this).balance`)
- [ ] Run `just test-dev --match-path test/dispute/DelayedWETH.t.sol -v` with higher fuzz runs (`FOUNDRY_FUZZ_RUNS=1000`) to stress-test bounds

### Notes
- Requested by: @aliersh
- [Link to Devin run](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5e66bf3514e64a46a3b50f565a8bc9e8)
